pr.title: Give CI reviews other repositories to read, through review.context_repos
pr.head: de00aedc520cc2d966e000a0d25d49b73dfe4ea5

summary: Projector can review a pull request in a GitHub Actions job, with no agent session running anywhere. Until now that review could read only the repository under review. So it could not check a call against the API in another repository that the call targets.

This pull request adds a committed setting, review.context_repos, that lists other repositories as owner/name. Before the agent starts, project review run decides which of them the review may read, clones each one it keeps at depth 1, and names their folders in the prompt as context, never as code to review.

1. The same owner. An app's installation token reaches only one account's repositories, so the review leaves out a repository of another owner.
  2. An app. The workflow's own token, github-actions[bot], reaches only its own repository, so under it the review keeps no context repository.
  3. Visibility. The review keeps a repository only when it is public, or when it and the reviewed repository are both private or internal, as a visibility check reported. A check that fails keeps nothing private.

The review's own token still reaches only the reviewed repository. The action mints a second token from the app, with contents: read alone, for the same-owner context repositories it reads from the default branch's setting. Because the list comes from the default branch, a pull request cannot widen what that token reaches. project review run checks and clones the repositories with it, then removes it from the agent's environment.

GitHub refuses the whole second token when the app cannot reach any one listed repository. So the step that mints it may fail without failing the job. The run then leaves every context repository out with one warning, and the review goes on.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Context repository: a repository the review reads to judge the change, but never reviews.
  • Installation token: the short-lived token a GitHub App mints for the repositories it is installed on.
  • Preset: how project review run starts Claude Code or Codex.
  • Context token: the read-only installation token the action mints for the context repositories, which the run uses and the agent never receives.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The first review, at ec469c1, requested changes with one finding. One listed repository outside the app's installation made the token mint fail, so every review job failed instead of warning and going on.
  • f6a59f9 fixes it. The context repositories now get a token of their own, minted with continue-on-error: true, and a refused mint leaves the context out. The second review found the finding fixed and posted a clean verdict.
  • de00aed merges main, which brings in the run labeling a pull request reviewing before its agent starts. Git combined that change with this one in run.py without a conflict, and the plan's one conflict keeps both § 9 bullets. An incremental review read the merge and posted a clean verdict.

groups.title: Choosing and cloning context repositories
groups.kicker: Which listed repositories a review reads, and how the agent gets them
intro: run.py holds all of the selection logic. parse_context_repos splits the setting, drops entries that are not owner/name, and removes duplicates. context_repos applies the owner, app, and visibility rules, with a warning for each repository it leaves out. When the action reports that GitHub refused the context token, it leaves every repository out. clone_context then clones what remains with the context token.

Each preset hands the folders to the agent differently. The Claude preset adds each folder with --add-dir and denies Edit and Write in it. The Codex preset adds no folder, because Codex's --add-dir makes a folder writable and its sandbox can already read every folder.

files.note: The rules, the clone, the preset arguments, and the prompt text.

checks.text: A failed visibility check returns None, which keeps only a public context repository. When the reviewed repository's own check fails, every private or internal one is left out.
PROJECTOR_CONTEXT_MINT is the outcome of the action's Mint the context token step. On failure, the run makes no gh call for the context and reviews without it.
These deny rules join the --disallowedTools list. They use the same //absolute/path/** form as the scratch folder's allow rules.
The agent starts without the context token. The plan's § 9 notes that a process of the same user can still read its parent's environment, so the token's read-only scope is what limits a misled agent.
The run removes the clones only when it made the temporary folder itself. In the action, PROJECTOR_CONTEXT_DIR keeps them under $RUNNER_TEMP.

files.note: Passes the setting to run.run, reuses the new workflow-login constant, and gives init's gate note to a self-hosted runner only when ci.hosted says so.
Tells a headless review to read context folders only as context and to change nothing in them.

groups.title: A token for the context repositories
groups.kicker: The action mints a read-only token for the context repositories, apart from the review's own
intro: The review's own token, from Mint the app's token, is unchanged: it reaches only the reviewed repository, with the permissions to post the review. On another repository, its pull-request, issue, and status writes would let a pull request steer the agent to write where it only reads.

A new step, Read the context repositories, runs after Set up Projector. That setup step points origin/HEAD at the default branch, so project config get reads the committed setting from there rather than from the pull request. The step reuses run.token_repositories to turn the list into repository names.

Mint the context token runs only when that list is not empty. It asks for contents: read alone and sets no owner, because an owner with no repositories would reach every repository the installation covers. It has continue-on-error: true, and the review step passes its outcome to the run as PROJECTOR_CONTEXT_MINT.

files.note: Adds the context step and the context token's mint step, and passes the token, its outcome, and PROJECTOR_CONTEXT_DIR to the review step.

checks.text: This read takes the tracked .projector.toml from the default branch, the same source project review run reads, so the token and the run filter the same list.

Checked against the first review's finding: a 422 from GitHub here no longer fails the job, and context_repos returns no repositories on failure before it calls gh. test_a_refused_context_token_leaves_the_context_out_and_the_review_goes_on covers it, and CI's check job passed on this head.
Only the review step receives the context token. test_only_a_read_only_token_reaches_the_context_repositories_and_the_agent_never_gets_it checks that no other step does.

groups.title: Documentation and the plan
groups.kicker: The setting's reference, its guide, and what the plan settled
intro: docs/review-in-ci.md gains a guide section, "Give a review other repositories to read". It covers the setting, the app and owner requirements, the visibility rule, the separate read-only token, and what happens when GitHub refuses it. The plan records what implementation settled in § 9 and marks § 6 step 4 done. The project stays in-progress, because live runner checks remain.

files.note: § 9 records the decisions, and § 6 step 4 is marked done.
